simple.meaning: זְבוּל (zᵉbûwl) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a residence.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Isaiah, Habakkuk, beginning at 1 Kings 8:13. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זְבוּל (H2073).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: זְבוּל (zᵉbûwl) / H2073 is traced through 1 Kings 8:13, 2 Chronicles 6:2, Psalms 49:15, Isaiah 63:15 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: I have surely built you a house of habitation, a place for you to dwell in forever.”

timeline.evidenceText: I have surely built you a house of habitation, a place for you to dwell in forever.”
But I have built you a house and home, a place for you to dwell in forever.”
But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol,‡ Sheol is the place of the dead.
The sun and moon stood still in the sky,
